name: AI incidents & governance
summary: An AI deepfake network posting 3,000+ videos with 22m views spread false trade and referendum claims in Canada
state: The OECD AI incidents monitor recorded on 12 Nov a network, likely based outside Canada, that used AI-generated deepfake videos impersonating Canadian influencers to spread false claims about US–Canada trade and local referendums; more than 3,000 videos reached over 22 million views, and TikTok removed some (OECD.AI). Malaysia's regulator said on 17 Nov it had secured removal of 13,883 deepfake items since 2024 (Business Today). A significant deepfake disruption keeps Watch; no AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure was found as of 26 Nov.
for_you: Treat viral political videos with caution and check them against established news outlets or official sources.
rubric_hit: Major deepfake disruption = Watch; no AI-enabled infrastructure attack or mass harm

sources.title: OECD.AI — AI deepfake network spreads political misinformation in Canada
Business Today — MCMC removes 13,883 deepfake content items since 2024

why: Powerful AI systems are being deployed faster than safeguards; serious incidents or governance breakdowns carry systemic risk.
drivers: Model releases, misuse incidents, regulation, compute controls, deepfakes in elections.

rubric.alert: AI-enabled attack on critical infrastructure, or AI-attributed mass harm event.
rubric.watch: A significant AI misuse incident, major deepfake disruption, or regulatory confrontation.
rubric.normal: No serious AI-attributed harm events or governance shocks this week.
